filename: TRENDS AND VARIABILITY IN THE OCEAN CARBON SINK.pdf
title: Trends and Variability in the Ocean Carbon Sink
testbed_rationale: This paper is a review article summarizing current understanding of trends and variability in the ocean carbon sink. It does not introduce a benchmark dataset or new ML parameterization testbed.
pain_points: Severe spatial and temporal undersampling of ocean carbon measurements (only ~3% of 1°x1° monthly grid cells have pCO2 observations), especially in the Southern Ocean, South Pacific, and Indian Ocean.
Systematic errors and uncertainty in extrapolation and machine learning interpolation methods caused by data sparsity.
Large discrepancies between surface pCO2 observation-based flux estimates and ocean biogeochemical models, particularly post-2010.
Uncertainty in air-sea gas transfer velocity parameterizations and surface skin temperature corrections.
Difficulty distinguishing natural decadal variability from anthropogenic trends due to decadal re-sampling intervals of repeat hydrography cruises.
extraction_notes: Review paper published in Nature Reviews Earth & Environment. Discusses previous work employing ML approaches (e.g., SOM-FFN / neural networks in Landschützer et al. and Gregor et al. incorporated into SeaFlux) for pCO2 spatial interpolation/gapfilling, but does not train or develop new ML models in this manuscript.
